name: AD826 (ADI high-speed, low-power dual video op-amp)
tagline: ADI's 50 MHz, 350 V/µs video dual. CD-player tweakers found it cleaner and more open than the AD827, and 'almost as good' as an OPA637.
technology: Bipolar high-speed voltage-feedback dual op-amp. ADI's macro-model uses an NPN input pair. It is unity-gain stable and ADI rates it to drive unlimited capacitive load. It runs from a single +5 V to +36 V supply or split ±2.5 V to ±18 V, drawing 15 mA max for both amplifiers. ADI's headline specs match the single-channel AD817.

reputation.summary: This is a niche op-amp for rolling in CD players, not a mainstream audio legend. ADI designed it for video, CATV, copiers, LCDs, scanners and fax machines. In the Audio Asylum 'tweaks' forum and on diyAudio, a few users who swapped it into CD-player output and I/V stages called the sound 'much cleaner, more open, and more detailed'. They also reported more precise instrument placement than the AD827, and one Audio Asylum poster found it 'almost as good' as the OPA637. Its appeal is video-class speed (50 MHz, 350 V/µs) combined with stability into capacitive loads. No independent measurements (Audio Science Review, Samuel Groner) were found. A 2005 translation of Tangent's op-amp notes (DiyEden/Soomal) put the AD826 on its list to test, but no review followed.
typical_uses: CD-player analog output stage op-amp swap
Video and line drivers (the designed use)
Buffers driving cables or capacitive loads
caveats: The evidence is thin: a few forum posts from the discovery notes, which were not re-read in this pass. There are no published measurements.

This is a 50 MHz video part. Tight decoupling and short leads are sensible when socket-rolling, although ADI rates it stable into any capacitive load. This is engineering inference, not a reported failure.
Input bias current is high (3.3 µA typ, 6.6 µA max), which can cause DC offset with large feedback or source resistances.
Voltage noise is moderate at 15 nV/√Hz, well above NE5532- or AD797-class parts.
It draws up to 15 mA per package (7.5 mA max per amplifier), so it runs warmer and drains batteries faster than audio duals.
The DIP versions (AD826AN/ANZ) are reportedly discontinued, so DIP socket-rollers depend on old stock or SOIC-to-DIP adapters.
The Tangent/DiyEden headphone-amp notes argued that ultra-high-speed op-amps are generally a poor fit for simple headphone amps.

counterfeit_notes: No reports of fake or remarked AD826 parts were found. The leaded DIP (AD826AN) and reportedly the AD826ANZ are discontinued per ADI PDN 10_0081 Rev. B (search summary). Any 'new' DIP stock is therefore old inventory or suspect. Loose 'AD826ARZ/AD826AR SOP-8, 10 pcs/lot' marketplace listings exist. Buy from authorised distributors (Mouser, Digi-Key, Newark) and check the ADI logo, the lot/date-code format and the Z (RoHS) suffix.

revision_chain_notes:
The only vendor is Analog Devices. No second source or acquirer re-issue was found. The known chain, oldest to newest:

(1) Original edition (Rev. 0 or Rev. A), c.1992–93. It is inferred from the SPICE model marked 'Rev. A 11/92, (c)1993'. No datasheet copy, footer or date was found, including by the targeted 'REV. A'/'REV. 0' 1993–96 search. MISSING.

(2) Rev. B, date unknown (before 4/10). The only candidate copy is Alldatasheet doc 48429: the PDF page is already listed and the HTML view has been added. It is 14 pages and 231 KB, against 15 pages for Rev. C, and a search summary again calls it Rev. B. The footer was not seen, so confidence is low. The adjacent Alldatasheet doc 48430 (AD826AN) may be the same edition. The Rev. B date and change list are MISSING.

(3) Rev. C, 4/10 (April 2010), footer D08950-0-4/10(C). Changes from Rev. B: Power Supply Bypassing became Power Supply Considerations, updated Outline Dimensions, changed Ordering Guide. It is still current in 2026 at analog.com (both the AD826.pdf and ad826.pdf aliases) and on RadioLocman (di=171829, whose revision-history page is at p=14, and di=121451). Alldatasheet doc 520354 (AD826ARZ, 15 pages) is probably also Rev. C.

Still missing: the original edition's letter and date, the Rev. B date and a copy whose footer confirms it, and any Rev. A between them. The best next step is Wayback captures of http://www.analog.com/static/imported-files/data_sheets/AD826.pdf from 2000–2009, which should hold Rev. B. Older ADI URL patterns (1990s) are not known and were not guessed.
